derek (eng-security): Heads-up: user request for deletion (uid=98765) hit a hard stop in the DSAR pipeline during the keystore rewrap step. KMS answered with NOT_FOUND for the snapshot ciphertext id. Not ideal.

anya (eng-infra): any logs? which service called KMS and what was the exact error?

:derek (eng-security): pasted log:```
2025-06-02T09:12:03Z ERROR dsar-runner flow=delete uid=98765 step=keystore_rewrap err="keystore:index-miss: ciphertext_id=backups/2025-06-01/snap-uid-98765 not in index"
2025-06-02T09:12:03Z WARN dsar-runner uid=98765 status=pending_deletion note="keystore_index_mismatch"
```

oz (sre): that path looks like the nightly snapshot. I remember the keystore index migration (keystore-v2) had a quiet mismatch list. Did that migration touch this namespace?

deploy-bot: migration mg-keystore-v2 ran 2025-05-31T23:58:12Z exit=0 mismatches=19 written=/var/log/migrations/keystore-v2-mismatch-20250531.log

anya (eng-infra): confirmed: mismatch log contains 5 entries where ciphertext path starts with backups/2025-06-01. Looks like index reconciliation didn't sweep newly created snapshots in that window.

tasha (legal): Legal: place a temporary preservation/retention-exception. We need to ensure we don't destroy evidence while we investigate. Please include case id RE-2025-401 on the ticket and cc privacy@redwood.

derek (eng-security): created RE-2025-401. Proposed short-term mitigation: 1) mark user record as pending_deletion (prevent user-store purge) 2) create legal retention-exception 3) run keystore-index-reconcile for 2025-05-30..2025-06-02 4) once reconciled, perform rewrap+delete.

anya (eng-infra): RBAC question: dsar-runner uses svc:dsar-worker which currently does NOT have keystore:read on snapshot namespace. Options: A) grant svc-dsar-worker temporary keystore:read, B) implement a keystore-rewrap-proxy microservice that holds keystore read perms and emits auditable events. I prefer B.

oz (sre): Agreed on proxy. Also require that proxy writes an immutable audit_event (audit-log) with: actor, target_ciphertext, operation, request_id, timestamp, result. That audit event must be retained per legal retention policy.

tasha (legal): audit events must include the request_id and signed integrity (we can accept HMAC signed by our evidence KMS key). Include a short chain-of-custody note: who requested, who acted, and why.

derek (eng-security): additionally we should add a defensive forensics path: if keystore index reconcile fails or key material is missing (KMS key DISABLED/DELETED), produce signed manifest (sha256) of stored snapshot blobs and place them in evidence-bucket with restricted ACL, record manifest id in RE-2025-401. Security to own runbook.

anya (eng-infra): small change to DSAR flow: if rewrap returns index-miss, don't immediately retry. Mark and enqueue for reconcile job and open incident stub with label dsar-keystore-index. That prevents noisy retries.

oz (sre): also add an oncall play: if the same uid gets index-miss > 2 times within 24h, page eng-infra and eng-security.

deploy-bot: note: we should add an integration test in snapshot pipeline: post-snapshot, write a test ciphertext and verify keystore index entry exists and a test rewrap to target key succeeds. Fail the snapshot job on mismatch.

anya (eng-infra): will add CI check and a one-off reconcile for 2025-05-30..2025-06-02. Estimate 3 hours. I'll prototype the proxy endpoint: POST /v1/keystore/rewrap {ciphertext_path, target_key, request_id} -> {status, audit_event_id}. Tokens minted via token-service with ttl=15m.

derek (eng-security): action items: - anya: spin up keystore-proxy PR + CI test - oz: add oncall paging rule + incident stub template - tasha: confirm legal retention-exception template fields we need (case id included) - derek: create forensic manifest template and evidence bucket ACL policy - ops-bot: ensure dsar-runner marks and enqueues instead of retrying immediately

tasha (legal): retention-exception required fields: requester identity, case id (RE-2025-401), affected UIDs, reason, hold owner, expected hold end (or indefinite), link to logs/audit_event_ids, signed statement if evidence exported. We'll need audit_event_id for each attempted rewrap.

derek (eng-security): noted. We'll include audit_event_id for each proxy call in the ticket.

oz (sre): one more edge: if KMS returns PERMISSION_DENIED, we must not grant broad RBAC to svc-dsar-worker. Instead use short-lived proxy token and rotate regularly. Keep principle of least privilege.

anya (eng-infra): agree. Proxy + short-lived tokens + immutable audit events + CI verification should reduce recurrence. I'll schedule reconcile job now and post status in RE-2025-401.

derek (eng-security): good. closing for the time being. Reopen thread if legal asks for exported evidence or if reconcile hits blockers. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
